blocks.text: NEW TESTAMENT
Simeon. The man in the temple who took the child Jesus in his arms, blessed God, and spoke to Mary of what was to come.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“Just and devout … and the Holy Ghost was upon him” (Luke 2:25); Luke does not call him a prophet

HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS

From the textLuke says nothing more of him. It had been revealed that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ, and he asked to “depart in peace”; Scripture does not record his death. Luke 2:26 Luke 2:29
TRADITION SAYS

An apocryphal gospel makes Simeon the priest chosen by lot in place of Zacharias after Zacharias was murdered: “the lot fell upon Simeon. For it was he who had been warned by the Holy Spirit that he should not see death until he should see the Christ in the flesh.”[7][8] Who says so: The Protevangelium of James 24 (apocryphal), ascribed to the 2nd century; known to Origen (Catholic Encyclopedia, 1907)
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Rabban Simeon, son of Hillel and father of Gamaliel
Michaelis, Paulus and older commentators (as reported by Meyer, 1880); J. Lightfoot answered objections to it (as reported by Gill)

The famous teacher Simeon son of Hillel lived at this time, and the Mishna passes over him; some have guessed that this was because he believed in Jesus. Gill sets out the case and leaves it “uncertain and undetermined who he was”. Luke 2:25 [25][26][24]
An unknown man
H. A. W. Meyer (English 1880); Matthew Poole (1683–1685), with Calvin and Brentius; F. W. Farrar (Cambridge Bible, 1880); E. H. Plumptre (Ellicott’s commentary)

Meyer: who he was “is utterly unknown”; Luke’s picture of an aged man does not fit Hillel’s son, and the name was very common. Farrar: a famous rabbi “would hardly have been spoken of so slightly”. Plumptre: “all conjectures are very precarious.” Luke 2:25–29 [25][27][28][24]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Luke 2
PASSAGES · 1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Luke never calls Simeon a prophet or a priest.
Luke does not give his age; that he was old is read from his words “now lettest thou thy servant depart” (Luke 2:29).
Scripture says nothing of his family or of his death.
